findings.description: The instance user_data embeds the RDS master username (aws_db_instance.catalog_db.username) and the master password (var.password) in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is stored in instance metadata, retrievable by any process/SSRF on the host via IMDS and exposed in the instance's user-data attribute, disclosing the database master credentials.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a publicly resolvable/routeable endpoint, placing the MySQL listener directly on the internet rather than confining it to the VPC; this is the network-exposure precondition for the database credential leak above.

storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS storage, automated snapshots and any subsequent snapshots unencrypted, so the catalog database contents are readable by anyone who obtains the underlying volumes or a snapshot copy.

The policy attached to catalog_app_role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", so a compromise of the web instance yields full control of every bucket, every EC2 resource and every database in the account, including the ability to read/modify data and alter network controls (privilege escalation and lateral movement).

The database security group allows egress on all ports/protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, so a compromised database or any host using this group can reach arbitrary external endpoints for data exfiltration or command-and-control.
